Indonesia Occupational Safety Law No. 1/1970: A Guide for Foreign Investors

Understanding the core legal foundation of Indonesian workplace safety, statutory employer obligations, labor inspectorate powers, and regulatory risk mitigation for foreign direct investment (FDI) operations.

Law No. 1 of 1970 Supreme work safety statute
Law No. 13 of 2003 Manpower statutory rights
Permenaker 11/2026 Modern labor inspection powers
Statutory Foundation

The Legal Basis of Workplace Safety in Indonesia

Occupational Health and Safety in Indonesia—officially termed Keselamatan dan Kesehatan Kerja (K3)—is governed primarily by Law No. 1 of 1970 (Undang-Undang No. 1 Tahun 1970 tentang Keselamatan Kerja). While enacted decades ago, this fundamental law serves as the constitutional backbone for hundreds of subsequent ministerial regulations (Permenaker) and decrees issued by the Ministry of Manpower (Kemnaker).

Law No. 1/1970 applies universally to any physical workplace within Indonesian jurisdiction where power tools, machinery, pressurized vessels, combustible materials, or elevated work environments exist. It explicitly places the ultimate legal liability on the Workplace Manager / Plant Director (Pengurus Tempat Kerja).

Direct Personal Liability for Plant Directors

In Indonesia, compliance is not merely an abstract corporate liability. Under Law No. 1/1970, the individual registered as the legal director or operational head of a plant carries direct legal responsibility for workplace safety violations, including potential criminal sanctions.

Key Legal Articles

Critical Provisions of Law No. 1/1970 Explained

Article 3 — Safety Requirements

Mandates comprehensive controls to prevent fires, explosions, structural collapse, occupational poisonings, and excessive exposure to noise, vibration, or hazardous radiation.

Article 8 — Medical Surveillance

Mandates pre-employment, annual periodic, and special medical examinations (MCU) for all workers, conducted by doctors certified in occupational medicine (Hyperkes).

Article 9 — Worker Induction

Requires employers to thoroughly train and brief every new employee, contractor, and transfer worker regarding hazards, personal protective equipment (PPE), and emergency protocols.

Article 10 — The P2K3 Mandate

Empowers the Minister of Manpower to mandate the formation of an Occupational Safety and Health Committee (Panitia Pembina K3) in high-risk or large workplaces.

Regulatory Enforcement

Labor Inspectors & Permenaker No. 11/2026 Enforcement

Statutory compliance is actively policed by Labor Inspectors (Pengawas Ketenagakerjaan) from provincial Manpower offices (Disnaker) and Kemnaker headquarters. With the introduction of updated inspection frameworks (Permenaker 11/2026), labor inspectors have heightened oversight:

  • Unannounced Site Audits: Authorized entry into any factory, smelter, mine, or construction zone without prior notice.
  • Sealing of Machinery: Immediate mechanical sealing (pembekuan / penyegelan) of unlicensed forklifts, overhead cranes, or pressure vessels lacking current SIA inspection certificates.
  • Stop-Work Notices (Nota Pengawasan): Issuance of binding legal corrective notices. Failure to remediate within statutory timeframes leads to prosecution under Indonesian civil and labor courts.
  • Accident Seizure: In fatal incidents, labor inspectors coordinate with Indonesian National Police (POLRI) forensics, freezing project sites during investigation.
Strategic Roadmap

How Foreign Companies Ensure Complete Compliance

To maintain an unblemished compliance standing with the Indonesian Ministry of Manpower, international enterprises must execute a five-point compliance protocol:

Compliance Step Governing Regulation Operational Deliverable
1. Staffing Permenaker 02/1992 Appoint a certified Indonesian Ahli K3 Umum
2. Committee Permenaker 04/1987 Register the bipartite P2K3 Safety Committee
3. Machinery Permenaker 08/2020 & 38/2016 Perform statutory Riksa Uji equipment testing
4. Personnel Permenaker 08/2020 Acquire SIO operator licenses for plant drivers
5. Audit PP No. 50/2012 Undergo certified SMK3 national audits
